JUDGMENT
The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident that occurred on 07-01-2023.

2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 07-01-2023 at about 8.45 a.m. the petitioner was standing by the side of hotel near Pratham International School, on Valepura gate, Varthur road, at that time the driver of Car bearing No. KA.01.ML.2779 driven the same at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, due to which he lost control over the vehicle and came to the wrong side and dashed against the petitioner and caused the accident.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Sahasra Hospital, Varthur, after taking first aid treatment he was shifted to Svastha hospital, Whitefield, Bangalore,
wherein he was admitted as inpatient for about 15 days.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy, aged about 25 years and he was working as a driver and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to continue his work and suffering from permanent disability.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
prays to award compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notices, both the respondents have appeared before the court through their counsels, but the respondent No.1 owner has not filed written statement.

Respondent No.2 - insurance company appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by admitting the issuance of policy to the Car bearing No. KA.01.ML.2279 and the liability of this respondent, if any, is subject to proof of the policy.
Further contended that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
Further contended that, the driver of the Car was not having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.

Further it has denied the age,
avocation, alleged disability and income of the petitioner.
Accordingly, prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of Car Reg. No.KA.01.ML.2279 by its driver, in RTA took place on 07-01-2023 at about 8.45 a.m. near Pratham Interna- Prathap vs Mohiddin.

tional School, Valepura gate to Varthur road, Kotur Bangalore?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what amount & from whom?
3.

What order or award?
5.
In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 14.
Also examined MRC as PW.2 and he has produced the documents at Ex.P15 & 16.

Further office boy of Swastha hospital is examined as PW.3 and he got marked the documents at Ex.P17 to P19 and also Dr Jawahar B K of Jayanagar General hospital and Dr. S A Somashekara of Victoria hospital is examined as PW.4 & PW.5 and got marked the document at Ex.P.20 and Ex.P21 & 22.
The second respondent insurance company has not adduced any rebuttal evidence.

6. Heard the arguments and perused the material evidence that are available on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under.
Issue No.1 : In the affirmative

;
 Issue No.2 : In the affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final orders  for the following:-

 ISSUE NO.1 :
8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed his affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as P.W.1.

In support of his case, he has produced true copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, statement of witness, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 7.
9.
On perusal of Ex.P1- FIR is registered on the basis of Ex.P2 first information statement given by one Mohan who is an eye witness and also an injured in the said accident.
The informant gave the information as per Ex.P2 to the police by alleging the rash and negligent driving and accident by the driver of Car bearing No. KA.01.ML.2279.
After the registering of FIR, the spot mahazar is conducted by the IO.
10. The contents of Ex.P2 & 1 is in consonance with the contents of petition about the rash and negligence driving by the driver of Car bearing No. KA.01.ML.2279.
At the time of spot mahazar, the IO has found that the car bearing No. KA-01-ML-2279 has dashed against the shop.
As per the contents of Ex.P3 mahazar, the said shop is after five feet from the road.
Thus, it is established that the driver of the car bearing No. KA-01-ML-2279 went out of the road and dashed against the shop.
This shows that the driver of car bearing No. KA-01-ML-2279 was negligent and thereby went out of Prathap vs Mohiddin.

Sk on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51969765/
3 the road and dashed against the petty shop.
The Ex.P5 is the IMV report wherein it establishes that the car bearing No. KA-01-ML-2279 has fully damaged in its front side.

Thus, the contents of Ex.P3 mahazar and Ex.P5 IMV report prima-facie establishes the negligence of the driver of car bearing No. KA-01-ML- 2279.
11.
The Ex.P6 is wound certificate and Ex.P9 being the discharge summary wherein supported the case of the petitioner about the alleged injuries and treatment.

Ex.P7 charge sheet came to be filed against the driver of Car bearing No. KA.01.ML.2279 for the offence punishable under Sec. 279, 337,
338 and 304(a) of IPC.

By producing these documents, the petitioner prima-facie established the occurrence of accident and also the alleged negligence of the driver of the offending Car bearing No.
KA.01.ML.2279.
12.

Wherefore in the absence of any cogent evidence which could rebut the assertions made by PW-1 on oath supported by Ex.P-7 which is the charge sheet and the documents annexed therewith, this court should not have any impediment to conclude that the said documents prima-facie suffice to hold that accident, occurred due to rash and actionable negligence on the part of the driver of Car bearing No. KA.01.ML.2279.

The view taken by this Court that the police records are prima- facie proof in support of the case of the petitioner, is supported by the decision rendered in Kishan Gopal and another Vs. Lala and others reported in 2013 (4) T.A.C 5 (S.C.), wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has categorically held thus:
In view of the aforesaid facts, the Tribunal should have considered both oral and documentary evidence referred to supra and appreciated the same in the proper perspective and recorded the finding on the contentious issue No. 1 & 2 in the affirmative.

sentences.text: But it has recorded the finding in the negative on the above issues by adverting to certain statements of evidence of AW-1 and referring to certain alleged discrepancies in the FIR without appreciating entire evidence of AW-1 and AW-2 on record properly and also not assigned valid reasons in not accepting their testimony.

The Tribunal should have taken into consideration the pleadings of the parties and legal evidence on record in its entirety and held that the accident took place on 19.07.1992, due to which Tikaram sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the same and the case was registered by the Uniara Police Station under Sections 279 and 304-A, IPC read with Sections 133 and 181 of the M.V. Act against the first and second respondents.

The registration of FIR and filing of the charge- sheet against respondent Nos.1 & 2 are not in dispute, therefore, the Tribunal should have no option but to accept the entire evidence on record and recorded the finding on the contentious issue Nos.1 and 2 in favour of the appellants.
(Emphasis supplied by me)

It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the inc ident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105, where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the rider of the offending van.

sentences.text: 13. In view of the ratio laid down in the authorities referred to above and applying the settled principle of law to the case at hand, which is further supported by the oral and documentary evidence adduced by PW-1, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident leading to this case indeed occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of Car bearing No. KA.01.ML.2279 resulting in petitioner sustaining injuries.
During the course of cross examination of petitioner, except a suggestion nothing has been elicited so as to disprove the case of the petitioner.
There are no material evidence to prove that the petitioner's negligence was the reason for the said accident.

As per the mahazar, the said petty shop is of the five feet of the road,
thereby the contention of respondent No.2 insurance company that the petitioner was standing in the road cannot be accepted.
14. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 07-01-2023 which is caused by the driver of the Car bearing No. KA.01.ML.2279.
There is no reasons to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
15.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by the driver of respondent No.1.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
a) PAIN AND AGONY:-
At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 25 years.
The Aadhaar card produced at Ex.P8 shows that the petitioner was borne in the year 1998.
The accident took place in the year 2023.
Hence, at the time of accident, the petitioner was aged about 25 years.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P9 petitioner was admitted to Svastha Hospital on 07-01-2023 to 10-01- Prathap vs Mohiddin.

Sk on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51969765/
5 2023 and again from 30-01-2023 to 31-01-2023 which shows that he sustained segmental fracture tibia right leg, iliopubic and ischio pubic frami fracture on both side and urethral injury and acute urinary retention and also he underwent CRIF with IMIL NAIL right tibia on 07-01- 2023.
Further he was admitted to Sapthagiri Super Speciality hospital from 24-04-2023 to 02-05-2023 and underwent end to end urethroplasty on 26-04-2023.
The PW.2 doctor also stated that as the petitioner has undergone end to end urethroplasty with pelvic fracture, the petitioner has erectile disfunction and has whole Geneto urinary tract.
By considering the nature of injuries and the period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.1,20,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.
b) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P11, amounting to Rs.3,66,266/- which are supported by medical prescriptions marked at Ex.P12.
These bills are not disputed by the respondents and no grounds are made out to disbelieve these bills.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitle by rounding off the same i.e., Rs.3,66,300/- under this head.
C & d) 'Loss of future income' and loss of income during laid up period:
The petitioner has not produced any evidence to show that due to the accidental injuries and because of the disability caused by the accident he is removed or left his work / job.
In the ExP2 complaint it is written as the petitioner was working as a driver in Pratham International School.
As pleaded by the petitioner when the petitioner had been to his work of driver of school bus in pratham international school, the said accident was caused.

Further the petitioner at the time of cross- examination stated that the school authorities has the documents of his attendance and also they will take his signature on attendance register and also on salary details.
It is very important to note that at the time of cross-examination the PW.1 stated that he is working as driver of school van in Pratham international school.
In spite of sufficient opportunity the petitioner has not produced any documents to show that he is removed from service and also he has not got the salary during the laid up period.
No evidence or documents produced by the PW.1 to show that he is not continued with his earlier occupation due to the disabilities caused to him.
This shows that there is no functional disability for the petitioner.
The petitioner neither chosen to examine the school authorities to show that he is removed from service and he has not received any salary during the laid up period.
The up to date account statement or the relieving letter is not produced by the petitioner.

The petitioner has not examined her employer/school authorities to prove that during the recovery period he was not getting salary and later he has left the job due to disability caused by the injuries of the accident.
No such efforts or evidence is placed by the petitioner to show that he is not continued with earlier job/avocation.
Even the petitioner has not produced documents to show that he has obtained leave for which he has not got salary.

In spite of sufficient opportunity the petitioner neither examined his employer nor produced any documents to show that, he has left the said job due to the permanent disability caused to him in the accident.
The account statement is also not produced.
The relieving letter or the copy of resignation letter is also not produced.
In this regard if he rely on Section 114 of Prathap vs Mohiddin.

Sk on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51969765/
6
Evidence Act which states as follows;
Section 114. Court may presume existence of certain facts.

The Court may presume the existence of any fact which it thinks likely to have happened, regard being had to the common course of natural events, human conduct and public and private business,
in their relation to the facts of the particular case.
Illustrations

The Court may presume - (g) that evidence which could be and is not produced would, if produced, be unfavourable to the person who withholds it;
When a party has evidence with him to prove the existence of few facts and if such party has not produced those documents and offers no explanation of non production of such evidence the adverse inference has to be drawn.

By applying the said principle of law in this case the petitioner has not produced any documents to show that, she is not continued in service, the adverse inference has to drawn by holding that, the petitioner continued in service.
The petitioner has not produced any documents to show that, he has availed the leave due to which he has got loss of pay.
By considering the same this tribunal is holding that, the petitioner has not sustained any future loss.

The learned counsel for the respondent relied on the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No. 2155-2014 dated 23.6.2020 reported in 2020 (4) KCCR 2621 between K. Nandish V/s.
United India Ins. Co. Ltd., and another.

United India Ins. Co. Ltd.

sentences.text:
In this case, the Hon'ble High Court has held as follows;
"7.

It has been contended by the insurer that despite Doctor having pointed out that petitioner has disability of 11% of the right lower limb 4% to the whole body, and observed in the affidavit that unless the petitioner is able to prove that the said disability has affected his earning capacity, he is not entitled for compensation under the head 'loss of future earnings'

Reliance is rightly placed on the judgments of this court in the case of United India Insurance Co.Ltd. v. D.C.Rajanna and Another [ ILR 2000 KAR 3443] and North West Karnataka Road Transport Corporation v. Babu @
Babusab [ 2007 (1) KCCR 654].

North West Karnataka Road Transport Corporation v. Babu @
Babusab [ 2007 (1) KCCR 654]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This proposition is indeed correct position of law.
Even in the present case, looking into the nature of work carried out by the petitioner, it cannot be stated that the disability he has suffered would affect his loss of earning capacity".
In this case no evidence is lead by the petitioner to show that he is removed from the service.
No proper explanation offered by the petitioner for non production of the documents to s how that after the accident, he is not working as a driver in Pratham international school.
Looking into the nature of work and the evidence adduced by the petitioner, it cannot be stated that the disability he has suffered would effect his loss of earning capacity.
Accordingly, the question of awarding compensation towards loss of future income does not arise.'
That is to say as the actual financial loss arising out of physical disability is not made out by the claimant, as such the petitioner is not Prathap vs Mohiddin.
As per Ex.P9 discharge summary, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 16 days.
As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P6 the injuries sustained by the petitioner are grievous in nature.
As per the evidence of PW.2 doctor and PW.4 & 5 doctor the petitioner sustained severe injuries and it lead to many complications.
By considering the nature of injury and the period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.
Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.80,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
f) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner has spent 16 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

But by considering the nature of the injury as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e.,
Rs.16,000/- in total.
g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injury sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
The evidence of PW.4 reveals that the petitioner has no reflex or voluntary control of the bladder and also due to the end to end urethroplasty with pelvic fracture, he has got erectile dysfunction.
The age of the petitioner was 25 years at the time of accident.
The PW.4 is an urologist who stated that the petitioner cannot control the bladder voluntarily.
This makes the petitioner to be uncomfortable to travel or to go out from his house.
The petitioner has to dependent on the sanitary diapers as he has no voluntarily control of the bladder.
The injury sustained by the petitioner effects the daily life style of the petitioner which in turn certainly effects and it creates discomforts in his whole life.

Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.2,50,000/-
under this head by considering that for whole remaining life, the petitioner has to dependent on the diapers.
h) LOSS OF MARRIAGE PROSPECTS :
The petitioner had contended that due to the injuries sustained by him, he is unable to find a fiance for marriage.

The evidence of PW.4 doctor witness goes to show that the petitioner has got severe permanent disabilities and also the petitioner has no reflex or voluntary control of the bladder and due to end to end urethroplasty with pelvic fracture has erectile dysfunction as there is no sexual function possible.
Obviously the matrimonial prospects of the victim/petitioner who suffered grievous accidental injuries, would also be severely affected.
To put it differently the marital prospects of the petitioner are bleak.
If a person chooses to be a bachelor throughout his life, it is his wish.
Whereas if a person is compelled to remain so because of an unfortunate accident then that will lead to mental agony.

In this regard in the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in 2021 ACJ 2645 in the case of Divisional Manager, National Insurance,
Prathap vs Mohiddin.

Company V/s Akash and another wherein it is held for loss of marriage prospects to the tune of Rs.5,00,000.

In the instant case also as the petitioner suffered with these kind of disabilities by following the above said dictum of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, since the petitioner is aged only 25 years, this court deems it fit to award compensation under this head and the same is fixed at Rs. 5,00,000/-.
i) Towards future medical expenses: PW.5 stated that the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants which may cost around Rs.40,000/-.
By looking to the nature of injury sustained the treatment taken, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.35,000/- under this head.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
a. Towards pain and agony Rs. 1,20,000/- b.

Towards medical expenses Rs.
3,66,300/- c & Loss of future income and loss of NIL d. income during laid up period:

e. Towards food, nourishment and Rs. 80,000/-
conveyance f.
Towards attendant charges Rs. 16,000/- g.
Towards loss of amenities Rs. 2,50,000/- h.

Towards loss of marriage Rs. 5,00,000/-
prospects i.
Towards future medical expenses Rs. 35,000/-
Liability:-
According to the petitioner the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the Car bearing No. KA.01.ML.2779.
The respondent No.2 in its objection statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the Car bearing No. KA.01.ML.2779.
No other grounds are made out by the respondent No.2 insurance company to consider the contributory negligence by the petitioner or violation of policy conditions by the respondent No.1.

Hence, the respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.2 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.1.
The petitioner is entitle for compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
The amount awarded under the head of future medical expenses does not carry interest as it is awarded for the future expenses.
Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.

17.

ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

opennyai_summary.facts: The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident that occurred on 07-01-2023.
opennyai_summary.issue:
